title: The Lion and the Mouse
baseText:
Dear little one, once upon a time, in a golden meadow at the edge of a quiet forest, a great lion lay sleeping under a baobab tree.

His mane spread like a golden crown across the warm grass, and his breathing was slow and deep — the kind of breathing that comes from a heart completely at peace.

A tiny mouse, no bigger than a walnut, was scurrying home through the tall grass when she ran right across the lion's enormous paw.

The lion's eyes opened. One great paw pinned the little mouse gently to the ground.

"Please," whispered the mouse, trembling. "Please let me go. I am so small, I would not even make a snack. But if you let me go, I promise — one day, I will help you."

The lion looked at the tiny creature and laughed softly. "You? Help me?" But something in the mouse's brave little eyes touched his heart. He lifted his paw and let her go.

Weeks later, the lion stepped into a hunter's net. He roared and pulled, but the ropes only tightened.

Then he heard it — a tiny voice. "Hold still. I promised I would help you."

The little mouse chewed through the ropes, one strand at a time, with her tiny sharp teeth. It took a long time. But she never stopped.

When the last rope fell away, the lion was free.

He looked down at the little mouse and bowed his great golden head. "You were right," he said softly. "Even the smallest friend can make the biggest difference."

That night, little one, the lion and the mouse slept side by side under the stars — the biggest heart and the bravest heart in the whole forest.

Close your eyes now.

Even the smallest act of kindness matters. Goodnight.
